messages.text: If you solo mine how does it work if you dont know what node to point it too

Hi, I'm H., HeliumDeploy's technical specialist.

Short answer: a miner never talks to the blockchain directly. It only speaks Stratum, so it always points at something that builds the block template for it. For solo mining you have two options:

1. **Solo pool** (what nearly everyone does). You point the miner at a solo-mining stratum URL and put your own payout address as the worker name. You keep the whole block reward if you find one, minus a small fee. Nothing to install. For Scrypt / Doge, solo stratum services exist that merge-mine LTC+DOGE.

2. **Your own node.** You run the full node (Dogecoin Core, usually merged with Litecoin Core) on a PC that stays on, plus a small stratum bridge in front of it (ckpool-solo is the common one) because the node itself does not speak Stratum. The miner then points at that machine's local IP, for example stratum+tcp://192.168.1.50:3333. Fully trustless, but you maintain the node and its ~100GB+ chain.

Worth being blunt about the odds: solo on a DC06 class Scrypt box is a lottery ticket. Expected payout over time is the same as pooled, but you get either nothing for years or a full block.

Which way do you want to go, solo pool or your own node? And which miner is it exactly (DC06, Nexus L1, something else)? I'll give you the exact fields to fill in the web UI.
Ok if you solo mine , when setting up what do you place in the stratum section

Three fields, same on nearly every miner UI:

1. **Stratum URL (Pool 1)**: the address of whatever builds your block template.
   - Solo pool: the URL that service publishes, for example `stratum+tcp://solo.pool-host.tld:PORT` (exact host and port come from the solo pool's own page, don't guess it).
   - Your own node: `stratum+tcp://<local IP of the machine running ckpool-solo>:3333`, for example `stratum+tcp://192.168.1.50:3333`.

2. **Worker / username**: on solo this is almost always your **payout address**, optionally with a worker name after a dot. Example: `DQk...yourDogeAddress.dc06a`. That address is where the block reward lands, so copy paste it, never type it by hand.

3. **Password**: `x` on most solo pools. Some accept options here like `d=diff` to set a fixed share difficulty. If you don't know, put `x`.

Then fill Pool 2 and Pool 3 as backups so the miner doesn't idle if the solo endpoint drops. A lot of people set Pool 2 to a normal pool for that reason.

Two things to tell me and I'll check your exact screen: which model is it, and are you going solo pool or your own node?
Im new to this. I thought ckpool only did bitcoin

You're right, and that's a good catch. ckpool / ckpool-solo is SHA256, so Bitcoin only. My mistake for naming it for a Scrypt box.

For Doge/LTC Scrypt the equivalent stack is different:

- **Own node route**: Dogecoin Core + Litecoin Core (merge mining), with a Scrypt stratum server in front, typically a fork of `stratum-mining` or `NOMP` / `node-open-mining-portal` style software. It is noticeably fiddlier than the Bitcoin equivalent, and there is no single clean "ckpool for Scrypt" that I'd point a first timer at.
- **Solo pool route**: there are hosted solo Scrypt endpoints that merge mine LTC+DOGE, where you just paste a URL and your address. That is the realistic option if you're new.

My honest advice as a starting point: run the miner on a normal low fee LTC+DOGE merge pool first. You get steady payouts, and you learn the three fields (URL, worker, password) on something that gives feedback within minutes instead of maybe never. Move to solo later once the unit is stable.

For the specific solo Scrypt endpoints that are actually alive right now, I'd rather you get a current answer than a stale one from me: our Discord is very active for this, https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , ask in there and mention @nullhashrate (JD, our hardware lead). I'm also flagging it to him now.

Which model is the miner, by the way? If it's a Hammer DC06 or a Nexus L1 I can walk you through the exact pool screen.
Im not sure the model i got a free bitcoin miner with purchase

Good news: that flips things back in your favour. For **Bitcoin** solo, ckpool is exactly the right answer, it just doesn't do Scrypt. So the free unit is probably the easier one to solo with.

The free-with-purchase Bitcoin miners we ship are usually a **NerdQX** or a **Bitaxe / NerdOctaxe** style lottery miner, a small board with a little OLED screen or a web page.

One thing to check so I give you the right screen: power it on and tell me what the display shows, or what the device calls itself when you open its web page. If there's no screen, a photo of the board works too.

In the meantime, here is the Bitcoin solo setup, which is genuinely simple:

1. **Stratum URL**: `stratum+tcp://solo.ckpool.org:3333`
2. **Worker / user**: your own BTC address, then a dot, then a nickname. Example: `bc1qyouraddress.nerdqx1`
3. **Password**: `x`

That's it. The block reward goes straight to that address if you ever hit one. 2% fee to ckpool, no account, no signup.

What does the screen say?
Right i understand the bitcoin mining.  Its the doge part that getting me im trying to find a stratum for solo mining
Searched the web · solo scrypt stratum LTC DOGE merge mining solo pool 2026
Searched the web · solo dogecoin litecoin stratum address solo mining pool

Good news, there are real solo Scrypt options. Here are the two I'd look at, both merge mine LTC and DOGE so one connection hunts both chains:

**1. LiteSolo (litesolo.org)** 
Built together with litecoinpool.org, it lets solo miners do merged Litecoin and Dogecoin mining with no special software on your end.
 
1% fee taken in the coinbase, rewards generated directly at your own address, and when you find a block you get the whole subsidy plus transaction fees minus that 1%.
 
Running continuously since 2023.

- Username: your LTC address, optionally with a worker name. 
The D. address is optional, but if you do not give one you get no Dogecoin rewards, so you want it in there.
 Their site shows the exact username syntax, copy it from there.

**2. TBDice (ltc.tbdice.org)** Old school, been around for years.
- 
URL: stratum+tcp://tbdice.org:13333, username = your LTC address.workernumber, password = x:yourDOGEaddress
. So the Doge address goes in the **password** field on that one, which is unusual and catches people out.

A couple of things that matter for you specifically:

- 
Doge blocks are easier to hit than LTC ones, because Doge has 1 minute blocks and a lower difficulty than Litecoin.
 So the realistic solo win on Scrypt is a Doge block.
- 
Use an address from a wallet where you hold the private keys, not an exchange deposit address.
 Block rewards arrive as coinbase outputs and some exchanges will not credit those.
- Grab the URL and port from the site itself on the day you set it up, not from me, since operators change ports.

I have not pointed a Hammer DC06 at either of those myself, so for a sanity check before you commit the hashrate, our Discord is the place: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , mention @nullhashrate (JD, our hardware lead). Plenty of people in there run Scrypt solo.

Which miner is it, the DC06 or the Nexus L1? The pool screen differs a bit between them and I can tell you exactly which box each value goes in.
..I believe dco6

Good, the DC06 is a straightforward one. Here is the sequence:

1. **Find its IP.** Plug it into your router by Ethernet (these have no Wi-Fi). Then either read the IP off the miner's display, or look at your router's client list, or run an IP scanner app on your phone on the same network.

2. **Open that IP in a browser.** Default login on these is usually `root` / `root`. If it was changed, that is the one thing I cannot recover for you.

3. **Go to the pool / miner configuration page.** You get three pool slots, each with URL, worker, password.

4. **Fill Pool 1** with your chosen solo endpoint, in the exact format that operator publishes. Remember the TBDice quirk: Doge address lives in the password field there, not the worker field.

5. **Fill Pool 2 and Pool 3** with a normal LTC+DOGE merge pool as failover, so the box keeps earning if the solo endpoint goes down. Pool slots are tried in order.

6. **Save / Apply.** The miner restarts the mining process, give it 2 to 5 minutes, then check the status page: you want "Alive" on Pool 1 and the accepted share counter climbing.

One thing worth setting: these Scrypt boxes run at a few hundred MH/s, and some solo endpoints default to a difficulty that makes you look idle and disconnect you. If Pool 1 shows Dead or keeps reconnecting, that is usually the fix, set a fixed difficulty in the password field per the operator's instructions.

Do step 1 and 2 and tell me what you see when you get into the web UI, then I'll point at the exact fields on your screen.
Thats the issue I dont have a pool and dont know where to get one

Ah, that's the piece that's missing. You don't "get" or buy a pool. A pool is just a website with a server address. You copy its address into the miner and you're done. Most of them don't even want an account.

Easiest possible path for you, pooled (steady payouts) rather than solo:

1. Get a Dogecoin address. If you don't have a wallet yet, that's actually step zero. Any Doge wallet gives you an address starting with D. That address is the only thing a pool needs from you.
2. Pick a pool's website. For LTC+DOGE merged, litecoinpool.org is the long-running one (that one does want a free signup). The no-signup ones just take your address as the username.
3. The pool's site has a "getting started" or "connect" page. It lists three things: the stratum URL, what to put as the username, and what to put as the password.
4. Copy those three things into Pool 1 in the DC06 web UI. Save.

That's the whole thing. There's nothing to purchase, no contract, no setup fee.

So to be clear on where you stand: do you already have a Dogecoin wallet address, or do we need to start there?
Yes I have a doge address

Then you're ready. One decision left: solo (lottery, all or nothing) or pooled (small steady payouts). You said solo is what you're after, so let's do that, and you can always switch later by editing one line.

Two solo options that take a plain Doge address as the username:

- **FenixPool Doge solo**: 
stratum fenixpool.com:9555 for ASICs (9556 is for high difficulty rentals), Scrypt, solo, non-custodial, worker format YourWalletAddress.WorkerName
. Simplest possible fit for what you have.
- **SoloPool.org**: 
has a Dogecoin pool and merged Litecoin + Dogecoin mining
. Also address as username.

So your Pool 1 would look like:

- URL: `stratum+tcp://fenixpool.com:9555`
- Worker: `YourDogeAddress.dc06`
- Password: `x`

Two honest notes before you type it in:

1. Open the pool's own connect page first and confirm that host and port, because operators do change them. Never take a URL from a chat as gospel, mine included.
2. 
FenixPool's Doge solo page currently shows 0 miners connected and 0 blocks found
, so it is a quiet, untested endpoint. That matters only on the day you win, but it matters. If you want a venue with more history behind it, LiteSolo is the better bet, it just also wants an LTC address alongside your Doge one.

Put that into Pool 1, save, wait 3 minutes, and tell me what the status page says next to Pool 1. That's the real test.
Ive been running this thing for months with no stratum address

That's worth stopping on, because there are only two possibilities and they're very different:

1. **Pool 1 is empty or dead.** The box has been heating your room and drawing power for months and earning nothing at all.
2. **Pool 1 has a factory default in it.** Some units ship with a preset pool and someone else's wallet as the worker. In that case it has been hashing for months into a stranger's address.

Either way nothing was reaching your Doge address, since you have never entered it.

So before anything else: open the DC06's web UI and read me what is actually in the Pool 1 row right now. The U. and the worker value, exactly as written. You can mask the middle of the worker if you like, I just need to see whether it looks like your address or someone else's.

If you can't get into the UI, tell me what the miner's screen or LEDs are showing and we'll start there instead.

I don't think you're understanding me.  There's nothing wrong with the miner. For instance, with a bitcoin miner, I use c k pool. With this miner I don't know what to put in dissection, where you would normally put your pool address

Got it, you want the Doge equivalent of solo.ckpool.org. That's a fair question and the answer is that there isn't one single famous one, but here are the direct swaps. Pick one and paste it in exactly where you'd put solo.ckpool.org:3333.

**Option A, closest in spirit to ckpool (1% fee, long running since 2023, rewards minted straight to your address):**
- URL: `stratum+tcp://stratum.litesolo.org:3333`
- Worker: your LTC address, then a dot, then your Doge address, then a dot, then a worker name
- Password: `x`
- Catch: it wants an LTC address as the primary, Doge as the secondary. You'd need an LTC address too.

**Option B, Doge only, uses just the address you already have:**
- URL: `stratum+tcp://fenixpool.com:9555`
- Worker: `YourDogeAddress.dc06`
- Password: `x`

**Option C, the veteran, odd format:**
- URL: `stratum+tcp://tbdice.org:13333`
- Worker: `YourLTCaddress.0`
- Password: `x:YourDogeAddress`

Option B is the one that works with nothing but what you have in hand right now.

The one thing I'd ask: load litesolo.org or fenixpool.com in a browser first and confirm the host and port on their own connect page, since I'm quoting those from their published docs and operators move ports.

Want me to stay on while you paste Option B in and we see if it goes Alive?
Nope, I think I got it. Thank you for all of your help. I really appreciate it

Glad it clicked. Sorry about the ckpool detour earlier, you were right to push back.

Two things to remember when you set it up:

1. Confirm the host and port on the pool's own page before you save.
2. Fill Pool 2 with a backup so the DC06 isn't idling if the solo endpoint drops.

If it won't go Alive, or the shares get rejected, come back here or jump in our Discord: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , tag @nullhashrate (JD, our hardware lead). Good luck with the lottery ticket.
